context_sensitive_titles_warning: 王 / 大王 / 寡人: Resolve by speaker and passage context (e.g., King Xi of Yan, King Zheng of Qin / Qin Shi Huang, King Jian of Qi, King Jia of Wei, or King Fuchu of Chu).
太子: Usually Crown_Prince_Dan in Yan/assassination contexts, but check non-Yan passages (e.g., Zhao crown prince in Shiji 43).
趙王: Resolve across reigns (King Xiaocheng, King Daoxiang, King Qian/Youmiu) rather than collapsing into one person node.
荊王 / 楚王: Distinguish King You, King Ai (Hao), King Fuchu, and Lord Changping by year and event.
相 / 丞相 / 將 / 將軍 / 太傅: Title/rank shorthand; map to the specific person node via surrounding names/context rather than guessing.
使者 / 燕使者 / 賓客 / 左右: Often unnamed envoys, retainers, or attendants; do not force onto a named person node unless identified.
三晉 / 諸侯 / 六國 / 天下 / 百越: Collective or macro-regional terms; decide explicitly whether to map to specific state nodes or exclude from person-level edges.
太后 / 先王 / 母家: Kinship or predecessor references; keep separate from active characters unless explicitly modeled.
Rhetorical allusions and historiographical citations to exclude from active action edges: 殷紂, 商容, 箕子, 箕左, 柳下惠, 管, 晏, 曹沫, 齊桓公, 白公勝, 要離, 聶政, 揚子, 鄒衍, 莊襄王, 周文, 武.
